summary: Scalable publication preserves deny-by-default client writes, trusted identity/membership/coverage authority, Member privacy and sealed completeness before atomic publication. Emulator evidence covers the new protocol and legacy endpoint isolation. This is a pre-production prototype with remaining operational hardening.

findings.issue: No client-write or self-granted completion path found. Schema 1 endpoints are explicitly barred from acting on schema 2 revisions; both create and update/delete denial are tested.
findings.recommendation: Keep trusted service and Rules changes coordinated; retain cross-version regression tests.

findings.issue: Per-request, per-chunk and per-revision ceilings are enforced, but there is no new per-account active-staging quota. Privileged cleanup exists but has no deployed scheduler.
findings.recommendation: Before broad production use, schedule cleanup and define tenant staging quotas, rate controls and cost alerts.

findings.issue: The existing two-Firestore-lookup model checks Membership and publication, not a third Company.active document. Receiver entry checks Company.active; direct SDS access relies on active Membership.
findings.recommendation: Use Membership revocation to revoke SDS access, and coordinate Company deactivation policy with Membership updates.

findings.issue: Rules and services are emulator-tested. New real-cloud deployment/load and physical mobile-device acceptance have not been executed.
findings.recommendation: Complete coordinated deployment and platform/cloud acceptance before broadly sharing the app.
